stage: k3 profile: NCCL small-message sweep at the exact decode collective sizes (serve down, both nodes)
tool: tools/nccl_decode_sweep.py + tools/nccl_decode_sweep.sh (vLLM PyNcclCommunicator, image dsv41-flash-exl3-sm121:canonical-e13, sha256:c81762335a12)
nccl_version: 2.30.7+cuda13.3 (vLLM pynccl and the sweep use the same libnccl; GDR disabled: libmlx5 50.0 lacks mlx5dv_reg_dmabuf_mr, so LL buffers live in host memory)
transport: single rail rocep1s0f1 RoCE, NCCL_NET=IB, CROSS_NIC=1, Ring LL at decode sizes under KEEP (TUNING log: 10240..81920 B -> RING LL, channels 1..7; all_gather logits 387840..1034240 B -> RING SIMPLE, 8 channels)

per_step_calls_from_trace.c1: target graph 80 AR m=4 + eager embed AR m=4 + draft graph 7 AR m=3 + eager logits AG m=4 + draft-graph logits AG m=3 + 2 engram AG (small, not swept); graph replays with collectives: 2 (target, draft)
per_step_calls_from_trace.c2: same with m=8 target / m=6 draft

method.eager: 300 calls queued behind a GPU spin, CUDA events per call (device time)
method.graph_and_gapped: 30 calls per CUDA graph; gapped = a 48 MiB (2x L2) memset before every call; CUDA events captured into the graph time every slot; with-calls and without-calls graphs replay alternately (A/B), 200 replays each, profiler off
method.steady_us: median over replays and slots >= 5 of (slot period with call - median slot period without call): the call's critical-path cost incl. any slowed neighbour
method.startup_us: sum of the first 5 slots' excess over steady: what one graph replay pays once for holding network collectives
method.modeled_ms_per_step: sum(calls x gapped steady) + sum(eager calls x eager median) + 2 replays x gapped startup (weights in nccl-weights.json)
method.reps: phase 1 ran 21 arms x 2 reps (rep 3 and phase 2 were blocked, see blockers); runs are tagged clean/contaminated by the spark1 GPU utilization seen before the run's containers started

contamination.cause: From 07:27 UTC a Playwright chromium from another Claude session on spark1 ran GPU processes (nvidia-smi type G, pmon SM 7-32% each, device util 20-92% with our serve down). Runs that started with >0% GPU utilization are tagged contaminated.
contamination.effect: keep-family gapped steady latencies read 5-25% higher in contaminated reps (keep AR m=4: 54.9 clean vs 62.8 contaminated); eager and graph_mixing0 cells moved < 3%

best_vs_keep.mechanism_observed: With mixing on, each captured network collective slows the neighbouring bandwidth-bound kernel: flush kernels ran 10-16% longer in steady slots and 20-25% longer in the first 5 slots (profiled diagnostic, rank 0 and 1 alike); with mixing off the neighbour slowdown was -0.2..-1.4% and the NCCL kernel itself 2-3 us shorter. The graph startup (first call of a replay) stays 300-800 us either way.
best_vs_keep.other_knobs: No other knob beats KEEP in the clean runs: PROTO=LL +0.46 ms/step (AG slower), Simple +1.03, LL128 +1.67, ALGO=Ring +0.18, allreduce:tree +0.94 (1 contaminated rep; global Tree is invalid for AllGather), NCHANNELS 1 +0.58 / 2 -0.19 / 4 -0.15 / MIN 8 -0.14 (c=2: all worse), NTHREADS 64..512 +0.05..+0.9, IB_USE_INLINE, PROXY_CPUSET big/little, IGNORE_CPU_AFFINITY, NET_GDR_C2C within +-0.3 (contaminated reps only). KEEP stays the right non-mixing set.

safety.docs: NCCL env docs (NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT, since 2.13): with mixing disabled, NOT supported: (1) one communicator used from parallel graph launches on different streams without serializing dependencies; (2) launching a non-captured NCCL collective during an outstanding graph launch that uses the same communicator, regardless of stream ordering.
safety.trace_evidence: r3 c=1 trace (and s5): the eager target-logits all_gather is launched on the host a median 45.4 ms (min 39.9) before the target graph finishes, and the eager embed all_reduce 32.2 ms before, in 100% of steps: rule (2) is violated on the TP communicator. NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT=0 alone is therefore unsafe for this serve.
safety.safe_design: Route non-captured TP collectives (torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing() False) to a second PyNcclCommunicator; the captured ones keep the first. Then no eager call ever shares a communicator with an outstanding graph. Alternative: per-communicator ncclConfig_t graphUsageMode (0 no graphs / 1 one graph / 2 mixing) via ncclCommInitRankConfig.
safety.serve_status: untested in the serve; needs the dual-communicator patch, run.sh FORWARD_ENVS entry, audit markers and a serve ABAB before any default change

blockers_not_run: phase 2 (mix0_proxy_big, mix0_bare, mix0_so0 = mixing 0 + NCCL_GRAPH_STREAM_ORDERING=0, plus interleaved keep/graph_mixing0 controls) and algo_tree rep 1

reason: spark1's GB10 GPU was shared with another session's Playwright chromium GPU processes from 07:27 UTC through 09:45 UTC (device util 20-92% with our serve down); rerun: scratchpad k3prof/run_sweep_phase2.sh and ARMS=<all> REPS=1 REP0=3 tools/nccl_decode_sweep.sh once nvidia-smi shows no other GPU process
